# Arca Go SDK — AI Context

> github.com/arcaresearch/arca-go-sdk — Go SDK for the Arca financial
> infrastructure platform (accounts, payments, perpetuals trading, real-time
> streaming, audit trails). Hand-written port of @arca-network/sdk (TypeScript).

go get github.com/arcaresearch/arca-go-sdk

Import path is `github.com/arcaresearch/arca-go-sdk`; the package name is `arca`.

## Conventions (Go-specific)

- Every method takes a `context.Context` as its first argument.
- Money/amount values are decimal strings ("50", "0.01").
- Coin ids are canonical `{exchange}:{id}` ("hl:0:BTC", "hl:1:TSLA"), case-sensitive.
- Market-data timestamps are Unix epoch ms; all others are RFC3339 UTC strings.
- Errors are typed; use errors.As. Base type: *arca.ArcaError (has Code, Message, ErrorID).
  Typed: *ValidationError, *UnauthorizedError, *ForbiddenError, *NotFoundError, *ConflictError,
  *InternalError, *ExchangeError, *OperationFailedError, *OperationStalledError,
  *StepUpRequiredError, *StepUpCancelledError.
- Order rejections: a venue refusal is a *ConflictError (409) whose Code is NO_LIQUIDITY (empty book —
  retry or use a marketable limit), MARKET_DELISTED (positions settled by the venue),
  MARKET_NOT_TRADABLE (halted or not yet live), MARKET_NOT_USDC_COLLATERAL, VENUE_RATE_LIMITED (the
  account's venue request allowance is spent — on Hyperliquid it is earned by cumulative volume traded,
  not by elapsed time, so waiting does not restore it and each retry spends budget the account has not
  earned), or ORDER_FAILED (refusal
  with no narrower code; the venue's verbatim reason is in Message). None are retryable as-is — change
  the request. A bad-input refusal (tick size, price band, leverage cap, min notional, insufficient
  margin) is a *ValidationError (400) carrying the same verbatim reason. *ExchangeError (502) means the
  request never got a verdict (connection reset, timeout, unparseable response) and IS retryable.
  Branch on Code, not HTTP status.
- Token-provider clients refresh ~30s before expiry, retry once on 401, and retry once on 403
  (FORBIDDEN / REALM_SCOPE_MISMATCH — cached token valid but minted for a different identity,
  e.g. after a signed-in-user switch; a 403-triggered refresh also forces the live WebSocket to
  reconnect). OnAuthError fires when a 401/403 survives the refresh — tear down and rebuild.
- An Arca instance is bound to the identity its tokens are minted for: on identity change call
  Dispose() and build a fresh instance with the new user's provider.

## Initialization

```go
// API key (backend)
client, _ := arca.New(arca.Config{APIKey: "arca_...", Realm: "my-realm"})
// Scoped token (realm read from claims)
client, _ := arca.FromToken(jwt, arca.Config{})
// Auto-refreshing token
client, _ := arca.FromTokenProvider(provider, arca.Config{Realm: "my-realm"})

client.Ready(ctx) // resolve realm slug -> id (also lazy on first call)
```

## Operation handles

Mutations return *arca.OperationHandle[T] (HTTP runs in background):
- h.Submitted(ctx) (T, error)  — HTTP response before settlement
- h.Wait(ctx) (T, error)       — blocks until terminal state
- h.WaitTimeout(ctx, d)        — explicit settlement timeout
- h.Predicted                  — *PredictedEffect (sync, optimistic)

PlaceOrder/ClosePosition return *arca.OrderHandle (embeds OperationHandle):
- order.Filled(ctx) (SimOrderWithFills, error)
- order.OnFill(ctx, func(SimFill)) func()
- order.FillSummary(ctx) (*Fill, error)
- order.Cancel(ctx, path) (*OperationHandle[OrderOperationResponse], error)
- order.Resize(ctx, newSize, path) (*OperationHandle[OrderOperationResponse], error) // sized orders only; unsized triggers rejected

## Intent -> method

| Intent | Method |
|---|---|
| Create wallet | client.EnsureDenominatedArca(ctx, EnsureDenominatedArcaOptions{Ref}) |
| Create any object | client.EnsureArca(ctx, EnsureArcaOptions{Ref, Type}) |
| Create info object | client.EnsureInfo(ctx, EnsureInfoOptions{Ref, Labels}) |
| Delete object | client.EnsureDeleted(ctx, EnsureDeletedOptions{Ref}) |
| Get object | client.GetObject(ctx, path) / GetObjectDetail(ctx, id) |
| List objects | client.ListObjects(ctx, *ListObjectsOptions) |
| Browse objects | client.BrowseObjects(ctx, *BrowseObjectsOptions) |
| Create isolation zone | client.CreateIsolationZone(ctx, CreateIsolationZoneOptions{Path}) |
| List isolation zones | client.ListIsolationZones(ctx, *ListIsolationZonesOptions{Prefix}) — active only; Prefix is a raw path prefix |
| Archive isolation zone | client.ArchiveIsolationZone(ctx, ArchiveIsolationZoneOptions{Path, Reason}) — the inverse of create; zone must be empty (no objects under its path, no balances owed against its boundary, nothing on chain) or it is refused 412 DELETION_BLOCKED naming what remains. Idempotent, no step-up, no force flag. Keeps the on-chain boundary so historical operations still resolve; operator-reversible |
| Object labels (merge) | client.UpdateLabels(ctx, UpdateLabelsOptions{ObjectID, Labels map[string]*string}) — nil pointer removes a key |
| Read folder labels | client.GetFolderLabels(ctx, path) |
| Set folder labels (overwrite) | client.UpdateFolderLabels(ctx, UpdateFolderLabelsOptions{Path, Labels map[string]string}) — full overwrite; empty map deletes all |
| Merge folder labels (delta) | client.PatchFolderLabels(ctx, PatchFolderLabelsOptions{Path, Labels map[string]*string}) — nil pointer removes a key, unmentioned keys untouched |
| Balances | client.GetBalances(ctx, id) / GetBalancesByPath(ctx, path) |
| Transfer | client.Transfer(ctx, TransferOptions{Path, From, To, Amount}) |
| Fund (dev) | client.FundAccount(ctx, FundAccountOptions{ArcaRef, Amount}) |
| Withdraw (dev) | client.DefundAccount(ctx, DefundAccountOptions{ArcaPath, Amount}) |
| Payment link | client.CreatePaymentLink(ctx, CreatePaymentLinkOptions{Type, ArcaRef, Amount}) |
| Estimate fee | client.EstimateFee(ctx, FeeEstimateParams{...}) |
| Idempotency nonce | client.Nonce(ctx, path) |
| Aggregation | client.GetPathAggregation(ctx, path, asOf) |
| P&L | client.GetPnl(ctx, path, from, to) |
| Equity history | client.GetEquityHistory(ctx, path, from, to, points, *HistoryScopeOptions) |
| P&L history | client.GetPnlHistory(ctx, path, from, to, points, *PnlHistoryOptions) |
| Operation detail | client.GetOperation(ctx, id, *GetOperationOptions) |
| List operations | client.ListOperations(ctx, *ListOperationsOptions) |
| Export evidence | client.ExportOperationEvidence(ctx, ExportOperationEvidenceOptions) |
| List events | client.ListEvents(ctx, *ListEventsOptions) |
| List deltas | client.ListDeltas(ctx, arcaPath) |
| Wait for op | client.WaitForOperation(ctx, id, timeout) |
| Wait for quiescence | client.WaitForQuiescence(ctx, interval, onPoll) |
| Realm summary | client.Summary(ctx) |
| Create exchange | client.EnsurePerpsExchange(ctx, CreatePerpsExchangeOptions{Ref}) |
| Place order | client.PlaceOrder(ctx, PlaceOrderOptions{...}) |
| Cancel order | client.CancelOrder(ctx, CancelOrderOptions{...}) |
| Resize order (sized only) | client.ModifyOrder(ctx, ModifyOrderOptions{...}) — unsized triggers rejected |
| Close position | client.ClosePosition(ctx, ClosePositionOptions{...}) |
| Position TP/SL | client.SetStopLoss / SetTakeProfit / SetPositionTpsl / ClearPositionTpsl |
| Open with atomic bracket | client.OpenWithBracket(ctx, OpenBracketOptions{...}) → OpenBracketResult{Entry, TakeProfit?, StopLoss?} |
| List positions/orders/fills | client.ListPositions / ListOrders / ListFills |
| Realm-wide fills (all objects) | client.ListRealmFills(ctx, *ListRealmFillsOptions{Market?, StartTime?, EndTime?, Limit?, Cursor?, Order "asc"(default)\|"desc"}) — no object id; each Fill carries ObjectID; asc + cursor = durable replayable log (cursor echoed unchanged on empty page) |
| Fill trigger context (self-describing) | Fill.IsTrigger (*bool: non-nil false = known regular order; nil = unattributable — external trade/liquidation), Fill.Tpsl "tp"\|"sl", Fill.TriggerPx — decorated server-side, no per-fill order lookup needed. Liquidation fills carry Fill.LiquidationKind "liquidation"\|"adl" (empty on pre-stamp liquidations). |
| Exchange state | client.GetExchangeState(ctx, id) |
| Active asset data | client.GetActiveAssetData(ctx, id, coin, applicationFeeTenthsBps, leverage); MaxBuySize/MaxSellSize include reversing and split as MaxBuyReduceSize + MaxBuyOpenSize (same for sell) — the reduce leg is never refused for balance, the open leg is what buying power gates. Empty on Hyperliquid. |
| Asset fees | client.GetAssetFees(ctx, id, applicationFeeTenthsBps) |
| Set leverage | client.UpdateLeverage(ctx, UpdateLeverageOptions{...}) |
| Add/remove isolated margin | client.UpdateIsolatedMargin(ctx, UpdateIsolatedMarginOptions{...}) |
| Set margin mode (cross/iso) | client.SetMarginMode(ctx, SetMarginModeOptions{...}) |
| Order breakdown (pure) | arca.ComputeOrderBreakdown(OrderBreakdownOptions{...}) |
| Order limits | client.GetOrderLimits() |
| Min order size (UI gating) | client.MinOrderSize(ctx, MinOrderSizeOptions{Market|MarketID, Price, ReduceOnly?, IsTrigger?, SizeToMax?}) -> {MinSize, MinNotionalUsd} (ceil to szDecimals; treats any reduce-only as exempt — the venue only exempts an *exact* close, so verify a partial trim clears the floor yourself) |
| Validate order size (advisory) | client.ValidateOrderSize(ctx, ValidateOrderSizeOptions{..., Size}) -> {OK, Reason, MinSize, MinNotionalUsd} |
| Trade summary | client.TradeSummary(ctx, id, *TradeSummaryOptions) |
| TWAP | client.PlaceTwap / CancelTwap / GetTwap / ListTwaps |
| TWAP limits | client.GetTwapLimits(ctx) / RecommendedIntervalSeconds(ctx, mins) |
| Market meta | client.GetMarketMeta(ctx) / Market(ctx, id) / ResolveMarkets(ctx, symbol, *opts) / ResolveMarket(ctx, symbol, *opts) / PreloadMarketMeta(ctx) |
| Mids/tickers/book | client.GetMarketMids / GetMarketTickers / GetOrderBook |
| Candles | client.GetCandles(ctx, coin, interval, *GetCandlesOptions) |
| OI history | client.GetOIHistory(ctx, market, interval, *GetOIHistoryOptions) — OHLC open interest + 24h ntlVlm + mark; intervals 1m/5m/1h/1d |
| Funding history | client.GetFundingHistory(ctx, market, *GetFundingHistoryOptions) — SETTLED funding observations {T, FundingRate, Premium, S}; no interval (event series); default 7d, max 30d; HIP-3 supported; not predicted (use ticker Funding/NextFundingTime) |
| Sparklines | client.GetSparklines(ctx) |
| Custody status | client.GetCustodyStatus(ctx) — `.Implementations` carries each custody proxy's resolved impl address + version marker (`Kernel`/`Coordinator`/`HLModule`/`SimModule`/`Vault`/`VaultBeacon`); gate compatibility on `moduleVersion` / `exchangeArcaVaultVersion` (surface markers), not on the stable proxy address. `Version` is nil when the marker read failed |
| Boundaries | client.GetBoundary / ListBoundaries / ListExchangeArcas |
| Register recovery key | client.RegisterRecoveryKey(ctx, RegisterRecoveryKeyOptions{...}) |
| Generate recovery key | arca.GenerateRecoveryKey() |
| Prepare custody tx | arca.PrepareLockBoundary/PrepareWithdraw/PrepareAssignRecoveryKey/... |
| Reconciliation | client.ListReconciliationState(ctx) |
| Invariant check | client.CheckInvariants(ctx, limit, realmId) |

## Watch streams (real-time)

All return a stream with OnUpdate(cb) func(), Updates() <-chan T, Ready(ctx),
State(), OnStateChange, Close().

| Method | Stream value |
|---|---|
| client.WatchPrices(ctx, *WatchPricesOptions) | map[string]string (+ Get/Prices) |
| client.WatchOperations(ctx, path) | Operation |
| client.WatchBalances(ctx, path) | BalanceUpdate |
| client.WatchObject(ctx, path) | ObjectValuation |
| client.WatchObjects(ctx, paths) | map[string]ObjectValuation |
| client.WatchAggregation(ctx, sources) | PathAggregation |
| client.WatchExchangeState(ctx, id) | ExchangeState |
| client.WatchFills(ctx, id, opts) | Fill |
| client.WatchRealmFills(ctx, *WatchRealmFillsOptions{FromCursor}) | RealmFillUpdate{Fill, Cursor, Replayed} |
| client.WatchFunding(ctx, id) | FundingPayment |
| client.WatchCandles(ctx, coins, intervals) | CandleUpdate |
| client.WatchOI(ctx, coins, intervals) | OIUpdate |
| client.WatchTrades(ctx, coins) | MarketTrade |
| client.WatchTwap(ctx, exchangeId, opId) | Twap |

WatchRealmFills is the realm-wide at-least-once fill stream: catch-up from
the durable log (ListRealmFills asc) from FromCursor, then live fill.recorded
tail; replays from its cursor on gap/reconnect/resync. It subscribes by event
TYPE (subscribe_events), not by watching "/" — a realm-root path watch makes
the server assemble a full-realm snapshot and hold a realm-wide valuation
watch this stream discards. Contract: persist
u.Cursor after processing, pass back as FromCursor on restart; process
idempotently keyed on Fill.ID (duplicates possible, loss never). Empty
FromCursor starts from now (no history). Delivery starts on first
OnUpdate/Updates/Ready attach.

Knowing when an exchange arca can trade: creating one returns before its venue
account exists, and until it does every trading call answers 503
EXCHANGE_PROVISIONING. Two events replace polling for it.
EventExchangeProvisioned ("exchange.provisioned") means the venue account exists
and its metadata is stamped, so the object stops answering 503.
EventExchangeReady ("exchange.ready") means the trading agent is registered on
chain and it can actually trade. Both carry RealmEvent.Exchange
(*ExchangeProvisioning: ObjectID, Path, CosignRequired, Tradable,
AccountAddress, AgentWalletID).

They are separate because on a cosign-armed boundary they are separate moments:
the account is provisioned, but its trading agent needs the user to co-sign a
grant, so provisioned arrives with CosignRequired=true and ready follows only
once that grant lands — minutes or days later. Treat the gap as waiting on the
user, not a stall. On an unarmed boundary both arrive together.

EventDepositDetected ("deposit.detected") is money seen arriving at a watched
deposit address before it has been swept and become balance;
RealmEvent.Deposit (*DetectedDeposit) carries it. Chain truth, not ledger truth
— EventBalanceUpdated is still what says the funds landed.

Aggregation sources: arca.NewPrefixSource(p), NewPathsSource(paths),
NewPatternSource(p), NewWatchSource(id).

Lower-level access: client.WS() returns *WebSocketManager (On(type, cb),
typed OnX listeners, OnGap, OnAuthenticated, OnRotated, EnsureConnected,
RotateConnection, Disconnect).

OnGap(func(missed int64)) fires on delivery loss, from either source: a hole
the client observed in the server-assigned deliverySeq (missed is exact), or
a server-sent stream.resync marker announcing that events were dropped before
they were sequenced — a loss no sequence check can see (missed is a floor of
1). Both mean the same thing: refetch. Watch streams already do this
internally; register OnGap only for state you track yourself.

Gapless rotation: the connection is proactively replaced before the
infrastructure's maximum socket lifetime severs it. A replacement is warmed
alongside the live one — authenticated, fully re-subscribed, confirmed by the
server — and only then takes over, so delivery never pauses. Automatic; nothing
to call. Config.ConnectionLifetime overrides the default (50m), and a lifetime
reported by the server wins over it. A pointer to 0 disables rotation and
outranks both, including a server-reported cap, so the opt-out still works on
the production fleet — at the cost of an unplanned reconnect. No status
change is emitted across a rotation and there is no delivery gap; OnRotated
fires for per-connection server state that the swap cannot carry over (watch
streams handle their own). WS().RotateConnection() forces one, returning false
when there is no healthy connection or a handoff is already under way.

## Admin (realm-less builder client)

```go
admin := arca.NewAdmin(arca.AdminConfig{Token: builderJWT})
admin.SignInWithGoogle / GetMe / Refresh / Logout
admin.MintToken / MintDeviceToken
admin.CreateRealm / ListRealms / GetRealm / DeleteRealm / UpdateRealmSettings
admin.CreateApiKey / ListApiKeys / RevokeApiKey
admin.ListMyOrgs / CreateOrg / GetOrg / GetActiveTerms / AcceptTerms
admin.ListMembers / UpdateMember / RemoveMember / InviteMember / ListInvitations
admin.GetCredentialScope / ListAuthAuditLog / TransferOwnership
```

## Step-up auth (412)

Set arca.Config.StepUpHandler (or admin SetStepUpHandler):
func(ctx, arca.StepUpChallenge) (string, error) — return a single-use step-up
JWT. The SDK retries once and never persists it. Returning an error surfaces
*StepUpCancelledError.

## Anti-patterns

1. Reuse a nonce path on retry; do not call Nonce inside a retry loop.
2. Always Ready(ctx) (or call any method, which is lazy) before relying on realm id.
3. Use canonical coin ids ("hl:0:BTC", never "BTC").
4. FundAccount/DefundAccount are dev-only; use CreatePaymentLink in production.
5. size is base-asset units, not USD. Min notional is $10 (GetOrderLimits()).
6. Isolated-only markets (MarginModes == ["isolated"], i.e. deprecated OnlyIsolated) require Isolated:true + positive Leverage when opening/increasing on PlaceOrder; a ReduceOnly close/trim is accepted without Leverage (uses the position's current leverage, never re-margins). Independent of HIP-3 — some HIP-3 markets (e.g. hl:1:TSLA) are cross-eligible.

## Chart history is already marked; `points` is a ceiling

GetEquityHistory and GetPnlHistory are ONE computation — same buckets, same
marking; P&L history is equity history minus external flows. Every bucket's
EquityUsd is that bucket's cash valued at that bucket's own mids PLUS
unrealized P&L on every position open at that bucket, valued at the same mids.
It is not settled equity carried forward and the marking is not limited to the
live point, so do NOT rebuild the curve from candles: a rebuild that projects
the CURRENT position backwards has no term for a closed position, a realized
loss, or a liquidation, and silently flat-lines the days before the newest
position. Status describes the CASH side's provenance, not whether the point
was marked — ChartCarried means no ledger event landed in that bucket, and such
a point still changes value as the market moves. ChartIncomplete is the
degradation signal (a mid was missing, or the position overlay could not run).
Deposits move EquityUsd and never move PnlUsd, so chart EquityUsd (present on
PnlPoint too) for "what is this account worth".

EquityUsd is FLOORED at zero and the floor never destroys the number. Exchange
accounts are the one class permitted to hold a negative balance, and a negative
balance is worse to render than a zero. When the floor clamps a point the true
signed value comes back as UnflooredEquityUsd; when it does not, that field is
empty — so its presence is also the only way to tell a floored point from a
genuinely-zero one. PnlUsd is derived from the UNFLOORED value: a signed
performance delta must not be flattened by a balance clamp.

`points` is a CEILING: the ladder picks the finest rung whose bucket count fits
inside it, so a 24h window at points=180 is served at 15m (~96 points). The
response describes its own grid via Resolution + BucketSeconds, with
ResolutionRequested set only when coverage forced a promotion. Reconcile two
sources for the same series by window and resolution — never by "whichever has
more points", which a client-side reconstruction wins every time regardless of
correctness. PickResolution/BucketMs/AlignDown make the count predictable
before the request.

## Folder labels: PatchFolderLabels merges, UpdateFolderLabels overwrites

Folders are virtual aggregations of arca paths, so folder labels live in their own store keyed by (realmId, path) and are surfaced inline on BrowseObjects rows. Three operations: GetFolderLabels reads the current set (empty map when none are set); UpdateFolderLabels REPLACES the whole set (an empty map deletes every label); PatchFolderLabels MERGES a per-key delta (nil pointer removes a key, unmentioned keys keep their value, an empty map is a no-op, removing the last key deletes the row). Prefer PatchFolderLabels whenever you mean to change some keys rather than define all of them — e.g. flipping a projection privacy label on a user folder. The server merges inside one transaction, so two concurrent single-key writes both land; a read-then-UpdateFolderLabels round trip loses whichever write commits first. Validation (32 keys, key grammar `^[a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-9._-]*$`, `arca.`/`_` reserved prefixes, 256-char values) runs on the MERGED result, so a one-key patch can still be rejected for pushing the folder past the ceiling.

## TP/SL is an OCO bracket; cancelled orders carry a reason

SetPositionTpsl stamps one auto-generated OcoGroupID on both legs; when either fills (even partially) the venue cancels the other and sets CancelReason="sibling_filled". Pass an explicit OcoGroupID (on SetPositionTpslOptions, SetPositionTriggerOptions, or PlaceOrderOptions) to build or reuse your own bracket — it is advisory metadata, forwarded to the venue but NOT part of the order signature. A CANCELLED SimOrder exposes CancelReason (one of user_requested, sibling_filled, position_closed, position_flipped, liquidated, position_gone, market_delisted, insufficient_margin), readable on-demand via GetOrder / ListOrders. insufficient_margin is the one to handle in code: placement checks margin but does not RESERVE it, so a resting limit order can become unaffordable while it waits, and the venue retires it after it has repeatedly reached its price unaffordably over several minutes. Treat it as "free up margin, then re-place", not as a transient error to retry blindly. Two placement rules match Hyperliquid: an ALO (post-only) limit that would immediately cross the book is rejected (use GTC/IOC to take liquidity), and a trigger set on the wrong side of the current mark (one that would fire immediately) is rejected.

Sized (partial) TP/SL: a TP/SL leg closes the WHOLE position by default (SizeToMax). To scale out a fixed quantity instead, set a base-unit size — Size on SetPositionTriggerOptions (SetStopLoss/SetTakeProfit), or StopLossSz/TakeProfitSz on SetPositionTpslOptions. A sized leg is a reduce-only partial (capped at the live position size). It is NOT exempt from the $10 minimum — only an exact close is — so size scale-out legs to clear the floor. Because a partial fill of one OCO leg cancels its sibling, SetPositionTpsl does NOT auto-link the two legs when either is sized — so a TP that scales out half does not cancel the stop guarding the remainder. Pass an explicit OcoGroupID if you deliberately want sized legs linked.

## OpenWithBracket opens a position + TP/SL as one linked normalTpsl bracket

OpenWithBracket(ctx, OpenBracketOptions{Path, ObjectID, Market, Side, Size, TakeProfitPx?, StopLossPx?, TakeProfitSz?, StopLossSz?, ...}) opens a position and attaches its reduce-only TP/SL triggers as a linked normalTpsl bracket (Hyperliquid parity). The entry and its trigger legs are submitted as a single signed batch to one operation (POST /objects/{id}/exchange/orders/batch): one signature links the legs. This is NOT globally all-or-none — Hyperliquid only guarantees whole-payload rejection for pre-validation failures. The trigger legs ARM ONLY WHEN THE ENTRY FILLS — they can't fire on mark price before the position exists — and the venue server-stamps a shared OCO group on them (the entry is excluded). Returns OpenBracketResult with one *OrderHandle per leg (Entry, TakeProfit, StopLoss), all backed by the single bracket operation; each handle's Filled/OnFill/Cancel targets that leg. Until the entry fills, a TP/SL child is NOT yet a live venue order (no venue order id — addressable only by its cloid); its handle matches fills by cloid, and cancelling it before activation cancels the parent bracket. At least one of TakeProfitPx/StopLossPx is required. normalTpsl is a FIXED-SIZE parent-order bracket: each trigger child defaults to the ENTRY's Size (a fixed-size leg of the parent order, NOT a whole-position SizeToMax trigger); set TakeProfitSz / StopLossSz for a smaller partial-close child. For a WHOLE-POSITION TP/SL that sizes to the entire live position (Hyperliquid positionTpsl), use SetStopLoss / SetTakeProfit / SetPositionTpsl instead — a separate trigger-only model with no entry leg that is not accepted here. Caveat: the bracket's legs share one server-stamped OCO group, so a partial TP fill cancels the SL on the remainder; to "scale out half and keep a stop on the rest", open the bracket with only the sized TP and attach the SL separately via SetStopLoss.

## Resize / ModifyOrder on Hyperliquid is a cancel-replace

order.Resize(ctx, newSize, path) / client.ModifyOrder(...) treats newSize as the new TOTAL order size. On Hyperliquid this is a cancel-replace: the venue cancels the old order id and places a replacement with a NEW order id, retaining the cloid. The platform re-correlates later fills/cancels on the replacement back to the original placement operation automatically. newSize must exceed the already-filled quantity (a resize at-or-below the filled amount is rejected). Unsized (SizeToMax) whole-position triggers have no size to amend and are rejected.

## Not yet ported (REST equivalents available)

Merged chart streams (WatchEquityChart/WatchPnlChart/WatchCandleChart) and the
derived WatchMaxOrderSize are not in this release. Use GetEquityHistory,
GetPnlHistory, GetCandles plus the arca ladder helpers (PickResolution,
BucketMs, ComputeChartRange) and WatchAggregation to build equivalent behavior.
